```{r}


suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(survey)

```




### FINITE POPULATION SIMULATION (N = 10000)
### From the Adrian Frich census 0f 2011, we used the metropolis Ekurhuleni, and the residential information of Boksburg as the reference for our proportions for the different residential areas. That is we shall start with proportions of the total population as townships (50%), mid-income (28%), and high-income (22%). These numbers may vary in current reality, but they are a safe estimate for the proportions of total residents in a study area. 

```{r}

set.seed(1852) 

N <- 10000
size_low  <- .5*N
size_mid  <- .28*N
size_high <- .22*N



c(size_low, size_mid, size_high)
sum(c(size_low, size_mid, size_high))

neighborhoods <- c(
  rep("Low-Income (Informal/Township)", size_low),
  rep("Mid-Income Suburb", size_mid),
  rep("High-Income Suburb", size_high)
)

incomes_low  <- runif(size_low,  min = 5000,  max = 15000)
incomes_mid  <- runif(size_mid,  min = 18000, max = 35000)
incomes_high <- runif(size_high, min = 45000, max = 75000)

all_incomes <- c(incomes_low, incomes_mid, incomes_high)

pop <- tibble(
  id = 1:N,
  strata = neighborhoods,
  Y = all_incomes
)

head(pop)
tail(pop)
```



```{r}



# Extract True Baseline Parameters using exact course rounding notation
Y_bar_pop <- sum(pop$Y) / length(pop$Y)
Y_bar_pop <- as.numeric(format(round(Y_bar_pop, 1)))

S2_pop <- sum((pop$Y - Y_bar_pop)^2) / (length(pop$Y) - 1)
S2_pop <- as.numeric(format(round(S2_pop, 2)))

print(paste("True Population Mean:", Y_bar_pop))
print(paste("True Population Variance (S^2):", S2_pop))



```



###  SAMPLE SIZE ESTIMATION AND SENSITIVITY PLOT


```{r}


# Define an error range vector for the x-axis mapping
Required_error <- seq(100, 2000, by = 10)
error <- Required_error

# Compute Cochran sample size curves across the four parameter scales
sample_size_100 <- ((1.96 * sqrt(S2_pop)))^2 / (error)^2
sample_size_100 <- sample_size_100 / (1 + (1/N) * sample_size_100)

sample_size_75  <- ((1.96 * sqrt(S2_pop * 0.75)))^2 / (error)^2
sample_size_75  <- sample_size_75 / (1 + (1/N) * sample_size_75)

sample_size_50  <- ((1.96 * sqrt(S2_pop * 0.50)))^2 / (error)^2
sample_size_50  <- sample_size_50 / (1 + (1/N) * sample_size_50)

sample_size_25  <- ((1.96 * sqrt(S2_pop * 0.25)))^2 / (error)^2
sample_size_25  <- sample_size_25 / (1 + (1/N) * sample_size_25)

```


### Sample size plot


```{r}

pdf("Sample size plot.pdf", width= 6, height=5)

plot(Required_error, sample_size_100, type="l", xlab = "Margin of error (Rands)", 
     ylab = "Sample size", yaxt='n', lwd=3, xlim=c(100, 2000), ylim=c(0, 1500),
     main="Sample Size Estimates by True Population Variance")
par(new=TRUE)
plot(Required_error, sample_size_75, type="l", xlab = "", ylab = "", xaxt='n', yaxt='n', 
     col="green", lwd=3, xlim=c(100, 2000), ylim=c(0, 1500))
par(new=TRUE)
plot(Required_error, sample_size_50, type="l", xlab = "", ylab = "", xaxt='n', yaxt='n', 
     col="blue", lwd=3, xlim=c(100, 2000), ylim=c(0, 1500))
par(new=TRUE)
plot(Required_error, sample_size_25, type="l", xlab = "", ylab = "", xaxt='n', yaxt='n', 
     col="purple", lwd=3, xlim=c(100, 2000), ylim=c(0, 1500))
axis(side = 4)

# Set our target 5% error line boundary threshold
e_target <- 0.05 * Y_bar_pop
n_target <- ((1.96 * sqrt(S2_pop)))^2 / (e_target)^2

k_interval <- round(N / n_target)


n_target <- N/k_interval

abline(v = e_target, lwd = 2, col = "darkorange")
abline(h = n_target, lwd = 2, col = "darkorange")
abline(h = N, lwd = 2, col = "red")

legend("topright", c("100% Baseline Variance", "75% Baseline Variance", "50% Baseline Variance", "25% Baseline Variance"),
       col = c("black", "green", "blue", "purple"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)

dev.off()

e_target
n_target
k_interval

n_target*k_interval

```

### Calculated sample size is 1000 households for a 5% error of (R1284.42)

### We also see that the N= nk, just like the notes suggest.



## EXECUTE ONE REALIZED PROBABILITY SAMPLE SELECTION


```{r}


set.seed(1852)
# Systematic selection execution
random_start <- sample(1:k_interval, size = 1)
sys_rows <- seq(from = random_start, to = N, by = k_interval)[1:n_target]
sys_sample   <- pop %>% filter(id %in% sys_rows) %>% mutate(w = N/n_target, fpc = N)


head(sys_sample)
hist(sys_sample$Y)

# SRSWOR benchmark sample draw
srs_rows <- sample(pop$id, size = n_target, replace = FALSE)
srs_sample <- pop %>% filter(id %in% srs_rows) %>% mutate(w = N/n_target, fpc = N)

head(srs_sample)
hist(srs_sample$Y)

```





## DESIGN-BASED INFERENCE (Manual Formulas vs Package Check)

```{r}



# Manual Calculations (Treatment under SRSWOR Approximation rule)
y_bar_sys   <- mean(sys_sample$Y)
var_y_sys   <- sum((sys_sample$Y - y_bar_sys)^2) / (length(sys_sample$Y) - 1)
sys_se_man  <- sqrt((1 - n_target/N) * var_y_sys / n_target)

# Formal Package Verification via Survey Objects
sys_design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~w, fpc = ~fpc, data = sys_sample)
sys_package_mean <- svymean(~Y, design = sys_design)


print(paste("Manual Sample Mean Estimate: R", round(y_bar_sys, 2)))
print(paste("Manual Standard Error:       R",
round(sys_se_man, 2)))


print(paste("Package Survey Sample Mean: R",
round(sys_package_mean, 2)))
print(paste("Package Survey SE Vector:    R", round(SE(sys_package_mean), 2)))


```





###  SAMPLING DISTRIBUTION SIMULATION


```{r}

B <- 1000

# Monte Carlo simulation using the native course replicate framework
sys_distribution_means <- replicate(B, {
  iter_start <- sample(1:k_interval, size = 1)
  iter_rows  <- seq(from = iter_start, to = N, by = k_interval)[1:n_target]
  mean(pop$Y[iter_rows])
})

srs_distribution_means <- replicate(B, {
  iter_ids <- sample(pop$id, size = n_target, replace = FALSE)
  mean(pop$Y[iter_ids])
})




```

```{r}

pdf("sample means.pdf", width=6, height = 5)

     main = "SRSWOR Benchmark Distribution",

# Add the same vertical reference line to show the truth location
abline(v = true_mean, lwd = 3, col = "darkorange", lty = 2)

# 5. Reset the plotting layout back to a single window framework

dev.off()
```

### CI EXTRACTION LOOP & PERFORMANCE SCORES

```{r}

set.seed(1852)

# 1. Running  loops t capture the standard errors for each iteration
sys_distribution_se <- replicate(B, {
  iter_start <- sample(1:k_interval, size = 1)
  iter_rows  <- seq(from = iter_start, to = N, by = k_interval)[1:n_target]
  iter_s2    <- sum((pop$Y[iter_rows] - mean(pop$Y[iter_rows]))^2) / (n_target - 1)
  sqrt((1 - n_target/N) * iter_s2 / n_target)
})




srs_distribution_se <- replicate(B, {
  iter_ids   <- sample(pop$id, size = n_target, replace = FALSE)
  iter_s2    <- sum((pop$Y[iter_ids] - mean(pop$Y[iter_ids]))^2) / (n_target - 1)
  sqrt((1 - n_target/N) * iter_s2 / n_target)
})


```



###  Derive the confidence interval limits (Critical t-value with df = n-1)
```{r}
crit_t <- qt(0.975, df = n_target - 1)

sys_lcl <- sys_distribution_means - (crit_t * sys_distribution_se)
sys_ucl <- sys_distribution_means + (crit_t * sys_distribution_se)

srs_lcl <- srs_distribution_means - (crit_t * srs_distribution_se)
srs_ucl <- srs_distribution_means + (crit_t * srs_distribution_se)



```



### Calculate all the metrics using simple base arithmetic
```{r}



# Empirical and Relative Bias
sys_bias  <- mean(sys_distribution_means) - Y_bar_pop
sys_rel_bias <- sys_bias / Y_bar_pop
srs_bias  <- mean(srs_distribution_means) - Y_bar_pop
srs_rel_bias <- srs_bias / Y_bar_pop

# Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
sys_rmse  <- sqrt(mean((sys_distribution_means - Y_bar_pop)^2))
srs_rmse  <- sqrt(mean((srs_distribution_means - Y_bar_pop)^2))

# 95% Confidence Interval Coverage Probabilities
sys_coverage <- mean(sys_lcl <= Y_bar_pop & sys_ucl >= Y_bar_pop)
srs_coverage <- mean(srs_lcl <= Y_bar_pop & srs_ucl >= Y_bar_pop)

# Average Confidence Interval Width
sys_avg_wdth <- mean(sys_ucl - sys_lcl)
srs_avg_wdth <- mean(srs_ucl - srs_lcl)

# Monte Carlo Standard Error of the estimated coverage probability
sys_mc_se <- sqrt((sys_coverage * (1 - sys_coverage)) / B)
srs_mc_se <- sqrt((srs_coverage * (1 - srs_coverage)) / B)

# Empirical Design Effect (Deff ratio based on empirical simulation variance)
empirical_deff <- var(sys_distribution_means) / var(srs_distribution_means)


# 4. final score
Metrics <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Empirical Bias", "Relative Bias", "RMSE", "CI Coverage Probability", "Avg CI Width"),
  Systematic = c(sys_bias, sys_rel_bias, sys_rmse, sys_coverage, sys_avg_wdth),
  SRSWOR     = c(srs_bias, srs_rel_bias, srs_rmse, srs_coverage, srs_avg_wdth)
)



```



```{r}


print(Metrics)
print(paste("Monte Carlo SE of Systematic Coverage Probability:", round(sys_mc_se, 5)))
print(paste("Monte Carlo SE of SRSWOR Coverage Probability:", round(srs_mc_se, 5)))
print(paste("Empirical Design Effect (Deff):", round(empirical_deff, 4)))

```
